kicker: The job hunt, event-sourced. Kisuke just asks what's pending.
description: A standalone job-application tracker built as a proper backend service — append-only event log, stage state machine, delayed follow-up reminders, and funnel stats computed from events instead of snapshots. Kisuke consumes it over HTTP and answers "what's pending this week?" Built ticket-by-ticket through PR review, one issue at a time.
detail_description: Job hunting generates exactly the kind of scattered state I built Kisuke to kill: applications in six tabs, follow-ups in my head, and no answer to "how's the funnel actually converting?" JobBoards turns it into one service — every application moves through a stage state machine, every change lands in an append-only event log, and stats are computed from the log so the numbers are always reconstructible.

The domain is deliberately full of real backend problems: idempotent webhook ingestion (atomic claim at the storage layer, not an in-memory lock), CSV import that upserts on provider identity, delayed BullMQ jobs that must distrust their own enqueue-time state, and median time-in-stage via raw SQL window functions.

It's also a deliberate workflow experiment: the whole build runs as a GitHub ticket board — one issue per ticket, one branch per issue, squash-merged only after a review pass covering correctness, failure modes, and TypeScript idiom. Master reads one commit per ticket.
In progress — foundation phase done, domain logic next. Ends with a multi-stage Docker deploy next to the rest of the Kisuke stack.
